name: run_python
description: Run a Python script inside a bubblewrap sandbox to inspect the target binary. The sandbox exposes the target ONLY at /workspace/binary (read-only); /scratch is writable case-local temporary space whose files persist across tool calls, including a full objdump saved as text, and the Host removes temporary by-products when the case ends while retaining its recorded Python scripts; the network is isolated; python3 standard library and binutils (file, readelf, objdump, nm, strings, xxd, od, hexdump, size, c++filt) are available, but NO third-party packages (no capstone/pyelftools -- parse ELF via subprocess to readelf/objdump or struct). Whole-binary objdump is allowed for global localization, but return only bounded candidates and narrow decisive windows on stdout rather than the full dump. Each call returns an observation_id and pending evidence_id(s); after the output has been returned in an earlier response, summarize any evidence you intend to cite.

script.description: Full Python source. Call binutils via subprocess. You may write complete output such as objdump -d to /scratch/full_objdump.txt, search it in this or later calls, and print only narrow findings on stdout (that becomes your evidence).

timeout_sec.description: Execution timeout in seconds. 0 means default 240.

max_output_chars.description: Cap captured stdout/stderr characters (head+tail). 0 means default 60000.

name: list_patch_sources
description: List the Host-approved files and functions from the post-patch source snapshot. This source is investigation guidance only and never creates citable binary evidence.

name: read_patch_function
description: Read one metadata-approved function from one post-patch source file. The result is bounded, line-numbered guidance and is not verdict evidence.

source_file_id.description: Opaque source file id returned by list_patch_sources.

function_name.description: A patch-related function associated with that source file.

context_lines.description: Extra source lines before and after the function.

name: read_patch_source
description: Read a bounded line window from one Host-approved post-patch source file. Use source_file_id rather than a path. Source output is guidance only.

source_file_id.description: Opaque source file id returned by list_patch_sources.

end_line.description: Inclusive one-based end line; at most 200 lines are returned.

name: search_patch_source
description: Search literal text within the Host-approved post-patch source files and return bounded line-numbered matches. Source output is guidance only.

source_file_id.description: Optional opaque file id; use an empty string to search all approved files.

max_results.description: Maximum number of matches to return.

name: summarize_evidence
description: Write or revise natural-language claims and verification locators for evidence returned by one earlier inspection-tool observation. This tool never creates evidence or changes the Host supporting excerpt, kind, polarity, or provenance. Every evidence item cited by a final verdict must be summarized first.

observation_id.description: The obs_XXXX identifier from the earlier inspection-tool result.

evidence_id.description: An ev_XXXX identifier returned by the specified observation.

claim.description: A concise natural-language statement of what the raw target-binary output establishes.

excerpt.description: One to twelve concise excerpt lines that help independently verify the claim. The Host validates structure, not textual correspondence with the observation.

address_ranges.description: Up to four inclusive binary address ranges that locate the claimed behavior. Use an empty array only when the evidence has no meaningful code address.

name: submit_detection_result
description: Submit a patch-presence status using summarized target-binary evidence ids, concise reasoning, and decisive addresses. The Host validates every cited ledger item before writing the artifact.
